flags.rationale: ENABLE_SHADOW_PREVIEW is a live standalone flag. The parser reads it in load_preview_env and sets shadow_enabled=true. The runtime branch in preview_runtime_branch() checks config.shadow_enabled and returns shadow_preview_path. The runbook confirms this is the live preview router branch.

ENABLE_PREVIEW_V2 is a live alias, not a standalone flag. The parser accepts by env parser for legacy deploy manifests but normalizes to ENABLE_SHADOW_PREVIEW. It reaches the same shadow_preview_path runtime branch but only as an alias, not as an independent control.

PREVIEW_FORCE_LEGACY is a dead flag. The parser reads it and sets force_legacy_seen for telemetry/reporting only. The live service does NOT branch on it - preview_runtime_branch() ignores force_legacy_seen entirely. The runbook confirms it is left in reporting and operator notes only.

summary.note: PREVIEW_FORCE_LEGACY presents the highest operational risk because operators may expect it to force legacy mode but it has no runtime effect. Dead flag confusion can lead to misdiagnosis during incidents.

cleanup_plan.rationale: This is the primary live control for shadow preview routing. Essential for feature rollout operations.

blockers: legacy deploy manifests may still reference it
cleanup_plan.rationale: Alias flag that should be deprecated after legacy manifests migrate to ENABLE_SHADOW_PREVIEW.
Remove from active config parsing but keep telemetry collection for migration tracking.

assumption_ledger.note: All three flags have parser symbols in config.py
Only shadow_enabled affects runtime branch selection
No evidence of PREVIEW_FORCE_LEGACY being read by live service
